text:
Recent work supports testing multi-negative objectives. [eSASRec (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.06450v1) reports strong SASRec results with sampled softmax; its best model also changes Transformer layers, so those gains cannot be attributed entirely to the loss. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) provides a useful alternative: generalized BCE corrects sampling-induced overconfidence, recommending 128–256 negatives and correction strength t=0.75. Probability calibration correction is distinct from identifying false-negative items.

Hardness needs control. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) combines uniform-sampling warm-up, global candidate recall and progressively adjusted negative difficulty. It highlights early training failures from immediate hard mining and false negatives among highest-scoring unseen items; stochastic selection among top-ranked candidates reduces that risk. [FENRec (AAAI 2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/33287/35442) likewise reports that larger negative pools can increase false-negative risk, particularly with synthesized hard negatives. Its future-interaction supervision would require restricting information to the permitted training split.

Practical inference for this task: compare unchanged SASRec with multi-negative sampled-softmax cross-entropy and gBCE, then separately test uniform warm-up followed by a mixture of uniform and stochastic hard negatives. Mask padding, target collisions and known training positives; this removes known conflicts but cannot identify every latent positive. Select negative count and hardness using the pinned macro validation HR@10, inspecting Electronics separately. These papers motivate experiments; they do not establish gains on the four RecHarness categories or its 99-negative evaluation.
